reason: The repro mechanism is wrong: ollama.AsyncClient.chat(stream=True) returns a lazy async generator and makes no HTTP request at await time, so a 500/connection error/'model does not support tools' surfaces during iteration and is humanized into an LLMErrorEvent (ollama.py:228-237), never a silent tool-less retry. The bare `except Exception: stream = None` (no log) only catches client-side construction errors (e.g. a Tool.model_validate failure on a malformed schema); a TypeError from an unknown kwarg recurs on the retry and surfaces as an error. Residual: a swallowed, unlogged exception, and the retry-without-tools fallback is effectively dead for its documented purpose. high -> low.

reason: The finding holds, and its scope is broader than stated. The static TS tables are not just an offline fallback: resolveModel returns DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_PROVIDER for any provider without an override even when the sidecar is up (model-selection.ts:119), and restored overrides are pruned against the static KNOWN_MODELS_BY_PROVIDER (model-selection.ts:76). A JSON default change therefore ships a stale model id to every user with no override, and a JSON-only new model is dropped on relaunch. The drift test compares only the two TS copies. Severity medium stands.
